one_month_reasoning: Window 2026-11-24 to 2026-12-23: no Intel earnings (Q4 reports late January). Scheduled or likely items: the Dec FOMC (Polymarket prices only ~3% for a cut by the January 2027 meeting [src 28], so little macro help), possible 14A/EMIB-T customer announcements (CEO: 'next two quarters' [src 2]) and more detail on the first 18A customer [src 23], the securities suit filed Nov 13 [src 22], NVIDIA's leadership turmoil and stake sale [src 24], and year-end tax-loss selling in a name down ~58% from its June high. The stock rose 16% on 2026-11-23 into $59.66 after a -50% two-month fall; short-horizon reversal after a big up-day offsets weak momentum, so we center slightly below spot (median $59.0) with a monthly sigma of 0.23 (86% realized vol / 3.5 = 0.25, trimmed for vol mean reversion), close to a symmetric spread.

downside.story: P10: memory-driven PC correction deepens (PC units ~-14% in 2027), Intel's supply ramp lags (units -6% vs base) and AMD's 2027 supply surge forces earlier price cuts (price -3% every year, margin through the same price path), foundry losses stall near 2026 levels, and the market re-rates Intel to ~31x. Base rate: after a >=50% round trip the 12-month P10 was -32% (all) to -48% (ex-1990s) [src 29]; 86% realized vol argues for the fatter end.

base.story: PC units -8% in 2027 and +5% in 2028; server CPU units +40%/+20% (TrendForce) with Intel units +18%/+15% from its supply ramp; DCAI price/mix +10% in 2027 (shortage) and -8% in 2028 (AMD supply, Arm), so DCAI is ~35.1B/37.1B at 41.7%/36.1% margins; foundry losses -6.4B/-4.3B; EPS ~$1.49/$1.73 after NCI; 40.1x P/E leg and a mid-cycle cross-check give $67.6.

upside.story: P90: PC correction ends by Q1 2027, server CPU units beat TrendForce's +40%, Intel's substrate and Intel 3 supply ramps faster (units +10%) while the shortage keeps prices +4% higher, named 18A-P/14A customers cut foundry losses faster; the market pays ~48x NTM EPS as in Sep 2026.

reasoning: Base-rates lane. Setup: INTC closed $59.66 after a round trip from $142.35 (June) and ~$120 (early Oct): the Q4 guide on Oct 29 ($15-16B, GM 38%) and the CFO's 2027 PC TAM -10% plan triggered a ~28% one-day fall [src 21,1,2]; NVIDIA turmoil and a securities suit followed [src 22,24]. Base rates (own computation on 38 surviving US semis/tech large caps [src 29]): after a >=50% fall from the 12-month high within 6 months of the peak, with the trailing year still positive (n=40, mostly 2000-01), 12-month returns had median +23% (ex-1990s n=29: +13%), P10 -32% (ex-1990s -48%), P90 +450% (ex-1990s +220%), and 1 in 3 were lower a year later; INTC's own Dec-2000 case returned +3%. Survivorship bias inflates the upside, so I center below the raw medians. Round 2: the supervisor found my DCAI revenue (+20% ASP 2027) and margin fade (to 33%) assumed opposite price paths, my Intel share 53->40% was a derivation TrendForce does not state, and my share count double-counted SBC. Rebuilt DCAI on one price index: industry units (TrendForce) x Intel relative supply (CFO substrate ramp) x price/mix (+10% 2027 on Commercial Times-reported 2026 hikes and a 2027 shortage; -8% 2028 as AMD adds supply per Lisa Su via TrendForce 2026-10-12), with margin = 1 - unit cost / price (unit cost up with TSMC 2027 wafer/packaging prices). Shares: CFO's 5.44B fully diluted, +0.4%/yr escrow only. Added the NCI claim (~1.1B/yr, CFO) the P/E leg had ignored, and a normalised-earnings cross-check leg (FY2016-25 median Intel operating margin 23.4% at a 22.1x peer median; S&P semis 14.7x on 10-30, ~33x a year before). Exit 40.1x on the gate-openable Zacks snapshots. FY2027 EPS $1.49 is +14% vs Zacks $1.31 because our DCAI margin rides the 2027 price path; FY2028 $1.73 is below the lone $3.23 estimate. Base $67.6; P10 $28.8 / P90 $126.4 sized to base rates (-48% ex-1990s P10) and 86% vol. I keep my DCAI FY2028 (~37.1B) below the supervisor's booked 47.9B: the booked path needs Intel to roughly keep unit share against AMD's 2027 supply surge and Arm ~30%, which no source supports.

drivers.label: Global PC unit market (index, FY2025 = 1.00)
drivers.source: Intel Q3 2026 call (CFO), TrendForce 2026-10-08, IDC Q3 2026 tracker via Computerworld
drivers.derivation: 2026: -12% (CFO Zinsner's 2026 PC unit TAM view [src 2]; IDC Q3 2026 units -20.1% YoY [src 19] fits a steep H2). 2027: -8%, between TrendForce's baseline low-single-digit notebook decline and its high-single-digit case if DRAM/CPU prices stay high [src 18], and Intel's planning case of about -10% [src 2]; memory stays tight through 2027 per TrendForce. 2028: +5% on easier comparisons and NAND/DRAM supply easing from H2 2027 [src 18]; low confidence. Other evidence-based builds: Intel's own -10% (pc_tam 2027 0.792, -2% vs ours), TrendForce baseline -2% (0.862, +6.5%).
drivers.why: PC units drive CCPG volumes; the memory-price shock is the 2027 swing factor

drivers.label: Intel client revenue per PC-market unit (price x share index, FY2025 = 1.00)
drivers.derivation: 2026: CCPG revenue Q1 7,700 + Q2 8,900 + Q3 8,097 [src 6,5,1] + Q4 6,300 (Q3 x 0.78, CFO 'down more than 20%' sequentially [src 2]) = 30,997; / (32,200 x 0.88) = 1.094 (price increases and 2026 channel build offset unit loss). 2027: 1.08 (-1.3%): H1 inventory digestion (CFO: correction Q4-Q1, maybe Q2) and Arm/AMD share pressure partly offset by higher CPU prices; 2028: 1.06 (-1.9%) as share pressure continues. Alternative: hold 2026's 1.094 (+1.3% CCPG 2027) or AMD-share-gain case 1.04.
drivers.why: captures Intel's share and ASP within the PC market

drivers.label: Industry server CPU units (index, 2025 = 1.00)
drivers.source: TrendForce 2026-10-22; Intel CFO; AMD TAM statement
drivers.derivation: 2026 +31% and 2027 +40% from TrendForce's server CPU forecast [src 17] (Intel CFO: >30% both years [src 2]); 2028 +20%, a slowdown from 2027 but inside AMD's 35%+ server-CPU TAM CAGR to 2030 [src 20] (dollar TAM includes price, so units below it); low confidence for 2028.
drivers.why: agentic-AI inference is lifting CPU attach; the economic driver of DCAI

drivers.label: Intel DCAI units relative to industry server-CPU units (FY2025 = 1.00)
drivers.source: Intel Q3 2026 call (CFO: demand exceeds supply, substrate capacity +40% mostly H2 2027); TrendForce 2026-10-22
drivers.derivation: Built from Intel supply, not from 100 - Arm - AMD. Intel DCAI units: 2026 1.28x FY2025 (DCAI revenue 27,040 / 16,900 = 1.60, over a 1.25 price/mix index); 2027 +18% (Q4 2026 exit run-rate ~8% above the 2026 unit average plus H2 2027 substrate adds, CFO [src 2]); 2028 +15% (full-year of H2 2027 capacity less share pressure). Divided by server_mkt_idx (1.31 / 1.834 / 2.2008): 1.28/1.31 = 0.9771; 1.5104/1.834 = 0.8236; 1.737/2.2008 = 0.7893. Implied unit share, using the low-confidence derivation 100 - Arm (>20%) - AMD (~27%) = ~53% in 2026: ~44.7% in 2027 and ~42.8% in 2028 (a derivation, not a TrendForce figure; Arm ~30% includes hyperscaler in-house CPUs Intel never sold into). Other builds: share held flat (0.9771 all years, DCAI +17%), round-1 100-Arm-AMD path to 40% (0.7378 in 2027).
drivers.why: Intel is supply-limited in a fast-growing server market; its supply ramp, not demand, sets 2027 units

drivers.label: Intel DCAI revenue per unit (price x mix index, FY2025 = 1.00)
drivers.source: Tom's Hardware 2026-04-24 and TechSpot (Commercial Times): server CPU prices +10-20% since March 2026; TrendForce 2026-10-12 (TSMC 2027 price rises, AMD to raise 2027 supply substantially)
drivers.derivation: 2026: 1.25 = server CPU list prices +10-20% since March 2026 [src 33] (about +15% on the year) and richer Xeon 6 / custom mix (~+9%). 2027: +10% (1.375): supply stays short through 2027 (CFO [src 2]; TrendForce Intel next-gen limited supply [src 17]) and the 2026 hikes carry into the full-year average. 2028: -8% (1.265): AMD substantially raises supply in 2027 (Lisa Su via TrendForce [src 34]) and Arm reaches ~30% [src 17], so as Intel's substrate adds land the shortage premium is partly given back (base rate: Intel DCG discounting in 2021-23 once AMD supply caught up). ONE price path: the same index sets DCAI revenue and, through dcai_unit_cost, the DCAI margin. Alternatives: hold 1.375 in 2028 (DCAI +8.7%, margin ~42%), full give-back to 1.25 (margin ~36%).
drivers.why: DCAI price is the swing variable for both DCAI revenue and margin

drivers.label: Intel DCAI cost per unit incl. segment opex (index, FY2025 revenue per unit = 1.00)
drivers.source: Intel FY2025 and 2026 segment results; TrendForce 2026-10-12 (TSMC 2027 +5-10% advanced nodes, +10-15% packaging)
drivers.derivation: FY2025: 1 - DCAI margin 20.2% (3,422/16,900 [src 7]) = 0.798. 2026: 1.25 x (1 - 37.7%) = 0.779 (scale absorbs fixed cost). 2027: x 1.06 (TSMC +5-10% advanced-node wafers and +10-15% packaging [src 34], tight substrates) x 0.97 (units +18% on fixed segment opex) = 0.801. 2028: x 1.03 x 0.98 = 0.8085. Margin = 1 - unit cost / price: 37.7% / 41.7% / 36.1%.
drivers.why: makes the margin follow the price path

drivers.label: Intel Foundry + All other operating income ($M)
drivers.derivation: FY2025 base Foundry -10,318 + All other 264 [src 7]. 2026: Q1 -2,300, Q2 -1,900, Q3 -1,674 [src 6,5,1], Q4 -2,150 (18A underloading and lower volumes, CFO [src 2]) = -8,024. 2027: -6,400 as 18A costs (down ~40% since Q1 per CFO) and external wafers (first 18A customer signed [src 23]) narrow the loss while 14A risk-production spend rises; 2028: -4,300. Low confidence; alternative: losses held at the 2026 run-rate (-8,000) or breakeven by 2028 (0).
drivers.why: the foundry loss is the gap between Intel's product margins and its reported margin

downside.story: P10: memory-driven PC correction deepens (PC units ~-14% in 2027), Intel's supply ramp lags (units -6% vs base) and AMD's 2027 supply surge forces earlier price cuts (price -3% every year, margin through the same price path), foundry losses stall near 2026 levels, and the market re-rates Intel to ~31x. Base rate: after a >=50% round trip the 12-month P10 was -32% (all) to -48% (ex-1990s) [src 29]; 86% realized vol argues for the fatter end.

upside.story: P90: PC correction ends by Q1 2027, server CPU units beat TrendForce's +40%, Intel's substrate and Intel 3 supply ramps faster (units +10%) while the shortage keeps prices +4% higher, named 18A-P/14A customers cut foundry losses faster; the market pays ~48x NTM EPS as in Sep 2026.

model_inputs.structure_note: Annual driver-led set (7 drivers: PC units, Intel client price/share, server CPU units, Intel DCAI relative supply, DCAI price/mix, DCAI unit cost, foundry+other EBIT) mapped into CCPG, DCAI and a plain 'Foundry and other net' segment (driven share 93% of FY2025 revenue). DCAI revenue and margin now share ONE price index (margin = 1 - unit cost / price). Value carried by a P/E leg (0.75) on the build's own GAAP EPS at the horizon less an NCI adjustment, plus a normalised-earnings cross-check leg (0.25, not driver-linked: computed from FY2028 build revenue at Intel's FY2016-25 median operating margin). No FCF-yield leg (FCF negative in FY2027), no DCF (not a neocloud), no SOTP (no credible listed foundry peer).
model_inputs.gap_note: Annual rather than quarterly set (time-boxed revision). Leg weights 0.75/0.25 are judgment, untested; the normalised leg lowers the target ~$4.3 (-6.0% vs the P/E leg alone, 71.89): over 5%, flagged for Kilian. k = 0.8 kept although INTC's own multiple sits on depressed EPS (k 0.6 = ~-8% on the target): flag for Kilian. Financing: another equity raise in 12 months judged <20% (~54B cash and investments vs ~4B FY2027 FCFF burn in our build); DOC warrants (241M shares if Intel owns <51% of Foundry) ~10%, not booked. Escrowed shares' mark-to-market is non-operating and excluded.
